stem: Which statement best distinguishes pH from EC in irrigation water?
choices: pH describes acidity/basicity while EC reflects overall dissolved-ion conductivity; neither alone identifies the complete water chemistry
pH directly identifies each dissolved nutrient while EC measures only water temperature
pH and EC are interchangeable measurements when the same meter is used
EC determines alkalinity exactly, so pH is unnecessary when EC is known
rationale: pH and EC describe different properties. pH indicates acidity/basicity; EC is related to the total ionic concentration and does not identify individual ions or replace pH.
